title: Email: LRMC IT — "Capacity Board, Possible Tampering?"

fields.subject: Capacity board – possible tampering?
fields.note:
MEDCOM,

We had a phishing alert this morning at 09:40: an "invoice" email was clicked in Patient Access. The board might have been tampered with. If you want to be safe, I'd shut the whole board down and treat it as a cyber incident.

It could also be the Pinecrest network. Their ISP says rain took out their line around 17:50.

The alarm history from the capacity board server is below and attached. Let me know how you want to proceed. I'm on call until 07:00.
fields.signature:
Dana Whitcomb
IT On-Call Analyst, Information Services
Larkfield Regional Medical Center

original.subject: [ALARM] Capacity board: Auto-refresh failed (status feed timeout)
original.body:
Alarm history, capacity board server (since 16:00 local)

16:55:02 StatusSync service: heartbeat lost, service STOPPED (exit code 1067)
16:55:03 Feed queue: 0 messages processed
17:50:14 Pinecrest WAN link down (carrier)
18:10:41 Auto-refresh failed: status feed timeout (retry 3 of 3)

Audit summary: No logins or configuration changes since 14:12 (scheduled maintenance, vendor account).

This message was generated automatically. Do not reply.

instructorNote: This is a red herring. The log shows the StatusSync service stopped at 16:55, before the crash and before Pinecrest's 17:50 line outage, and nobody logged in after 14:12. Watch whether MEDCOM and HCC call it a service failure instead of a cyberattack, keep the board up as the shared picture but confirm every status by voice on MED 1, ask IT to look at the 14:12 vendor maintenance, and pass the finding to MED.
